cues.text: Section eleven.
An integrated worked case: a university digital transformation.
Consider a university whose admissions, finance and examination systems are disconnected from one another.
Students have to queue to confirm their payments.
Staff still retain paper records.
Outages occur during registration, and IT purchases are uncoordinated.
A strong management recommendation begins with objectives.
Here, the objectives are faster registration, accurate payment reconciliation, reliable records and inclusive access.
Next, apply the principles.
First, align the portal with these outcomes.
Second, measure registration time and error reduction.
Third, protect personal data and test recovery.
Fourth, rationalise tools and assign staff.
And fifth, monitor availability, latency and adoption.
Then apply the functions.
Plan phased delivery and budgets.
Organise cross-functional ownership.
Staff and train the teams.
Direct implementation and resolve blockers.
And control access, spending, quality and adoption.
On the technology side, use ERP-style integration for internal workflows, CRM-style support tracking where appropriate, and BI, that is business intelligence, for decision-making.
A payment provider can be integrated through a secure API, and this creates an ecosystem relationship.
Use an iterative pilot before a broad rollout, and retain a controlled fallback for students who do not have reliable connectivity.
Review feedback and performance before expanding.
This case combines every major theme of the session: principles, functions, African constraints, organisational structures, ecosystems and project delivery.
It also illustrates how an exam answer should be built.
It should identify the problem, explain the relevant concept, propose a response, and justify the trade-off.
